frs_sections.title: ABSTRACT / OVERVIEW
frs_sections.content:
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

The Expanded Serial Peripheral Interface (xSPI), standardized by JEDEC as
JESD251, defines an EXPANSION of the classic Serial Peripheral Interface (SPI)
for high-throughput access to serial NOR flash, serial NAND, and PSRAM memory
devices. Where classic single-IO SPI uses a bare four-wire full-duplex shift
register (SCLK, single MOSI output, single MISO input, and a chip-select CS#),
xSPI / Quad SPI (QSPI) / Octal SPI (OSPI) widen the data path to MULTIPLE
bidirectional data lines and add a structured command protocol: an instruction
phase, an address phase, optional mode/alternate bits, programmable DUMMY
CYCLES, and a data phase. This is the key structural difference from plain
single-IO SPI: QSPI/OSPI is a…

frs_sections.title: KEY FEATURES
frs_sections.content:
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

- Expansion of classic SPI for NOR flash / NAND / PSRAM (JEDEC xSPI / JESD251).
- Multi-IO data path: Single (IO0=MOSI / IO1=MISO), Dual (IO0-IO1), Quad
  (IO0-IO3), Octal (IO0-IO7 / DQ0-DQ7, "x8").
- In Quad mode, the classic /WP (write-protect) pin is repurposed as IO2 and the
  classic /HOLD (or /RESET) pin is repurposed as IO3.
- Structured command protocol: instruction phase -> address phase -> mode /
  alternate bits -> programmable DUMMY CYCLES -> data phase.
- Protocol-mode notation S-A-D, e.g. 1-1-1, 1-1-4, 1-4-4, 4-4-4, 8-8-8,
  8D-8D-8D (lanes used for instruction / address / data respectively).
- SDR and DDR (DTR) signaling; data on one edge (SDR) or both edges (DDR).
- Optional Data Strobe (DQS) …

frs_sections.title: PIN / SIGNAL DESCRIPTION
frs_sections.content:
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  SCLK   - Serial clock, driven by the controller (master). Up to 133-200+ MHz.
  CS#    - Active-low chip select (slave select). Frames each command;
           transaction is bounded by CS# falling then rising.
  IO0    - Data line 0. In single mode this is MOSI (controller output).
  IO1    - Data line 1. In single mode this is MISO (controller input).
  IO2    - Data line 2 (Quad/Octal). Repurposed from the classic /WP pin.
  IO3    - Data line 3 (Quad/Octal). Repurposed from the classic /HOLD or
           /RESET pin.
  IO4..IO7 (or DQ4..DQ7) - Data lines 4-7 (Octal "x8" only).
  DQS    - Data strobe (optional, octal DDR). Source-synchronous read strobe,
           edge-aligned to read data.
  RESET# - H…

frs_sections.title: CONTINUOUS READ MODE / XIP
frs_sections.content:
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

In a Quad/Octal I/O Read (e.g. 0xEB, 1-4-4) the controller can set the MODE bits
(alternate bits) after the address so that the NEXT read transaction may skip
the instruction phase entirely — the device stays in "continuous read" and
expects only address + dummy + data. This supports eXecute-In-Place (XIP), where
a CPU fetches code directly from the flash through the QSPI/OSPI controller's
memory-mapped window without explicit command overhead per access.

frs_sections.title: ELECTRICAL / TIMING
frs_sections.content:
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  SCLK frequency : up to 133 MHz typical (SDR), 166-200+ MHz on fast devices.
  Mode           : SPI Mode 0 (CPOL=0, CPHA=0) and Mode 3 (CPOL=1, CPHA=1) for
                   single-IO compatibility; multi-IO phases capture per the
                   device dummy-cycle and DQS configuration.
  Signaling      : single-ended CMOS/LVCMOS; push-pull on actively-driven lines.
  CS# setup/hold : device-specific; CS# must remain low for the whole command.
  Bit order      : MSB-first on each data line.

frs_sections.title: ERROR / ROBUSTNESS
frs_sections.content:
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  - WIP (Write In Progress) polling detects program/erase completion.
  - WEL must be set before program/erase; otherwise the operation is ignored.
  - Block / sector protection bits (BP) guard regions from accidental erase.
  - Wrong dummy-cycle configuration corrupts high-frequency multi-IO reads
    (the most common QSPI/OSPI bring-up error).
  - CRC / ECC is device-specific (some xSPI NOR add internal ECC); the bus
    protocol itself has no transaction CRC (unlike SMBus PEC).

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

frs_sections.content:
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  Quad SPI (vendor)        ~2010  Multi-IO 1-1-4 / 1-4-4 / 4-4-4 reads added
                                   over classic SPI NOR flash.
  SFDP (JESD216)           2011   Serial Flash Discoverable Parameters table.
  Octal SPI (vendor)       ~2017  x8 IO0-IO7, octal SDR/DDR.
  xSPI (JESD251)           2020   JEDEC standardization of expanded SPI: octal
                                   DDR (8D-8D-8D), DQS, command extension,
                                   register interface, variable latency.
  JESD251-1                2021   xSPI profile / addendum.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

frs_sections.title: USE CASES
frs_sections.content:
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  - Code-shadow / XIP boot from serial NOR flash for MCUs and SoCs.
  - High-bandwidth firmware and look-up-table storage via octal DDR.
  - PSRAM expansion memory over the same QSPI/OSPI controller.
  - FPGA configuration flash.
  - Automotive / industrial code storage with SFDP auto-configuration.

protocol_overview.duplex: half-duplex per phase (the bidirectional data lines IO0..IO7 are driven by one end at a time; instruction/address/data phases are directional). The single-IO 1-1-1 compatibility mode uses the classic full-duplex MOSI/MISO pair.
protocol_overview.type: Expanded multi-IO Serial Peripheral Interface (xSPI / QSPI / OSPI, JESD251) for NOR flash / NAND / PSRAM: a controller-driven SCLK + CS# interface with multiple bidirectional data lines (IO0..IO3 Quad / IO0..IO7 Octal) and a structured instruction-address-dummy-data phase protocol with programmable dummy cycles, SDR/DDR signaling, and a standard JEDEC flash command set.

sfdp.name: Serial Flash Discoverable Parameters
sfdp.purpose: self-describing capability tables for controller auto-configuration of read mode and dummy cycles.

compliance_requirements: Single-IO (1-1-1) SPI Mode-0/Mode-3 compatibility on SCLK/CS#/IO0/IO1.
Correct phase sequencing: instruction -> address -> mode -> dummy -> data, with the configured dummy-cycle count per read mode.
Support the claimed multi-IO modes (Dual/Quad/Octal) and SDR/DDR.
Implement the mandatory flash command subset and WIP/WEL handshake.
Where claimed: SFDP (JESD216) tables for self-description.
Where claimed (xSPI): octal DDR 8D-8D-8D with DQS, command extension, and the configuration-register interface.

auto_cited_sections.heading: PROTOCOL STRUCTURE — COMMAND / ADDRESS / DUMMY / DATA PHASES
INSTRUCTION phase : 8-bit (or 16-bit extended in octal) command opcode.
ADDRESS phase     : 3 bytes (24-bit) or 4 bytes (32-bit) memory address.
MODE / ALTERNATE  : optional mode bits (continuous-read / XIP hint).
DUMMY CYCLES      : a programmable number of clock cycles with no data,
DATA phase        : one or more data bytes, read or written.

functional_requirements.text: QSPI/OSPI shares SCLK and CS# with classic SPI and is Mode-0/Mode-3 compatible in single-IO (1-1-1) commands; IO0 is MOSI and IO1 is MISO in single mode.
The data path widens to multiple bidirectional data lines: Dual (IO0-IO1), Quad (IO0-IO3, with /WP->IO2 and /HOLD->IO3), and Octal (IO0-IO7 / DQ0-DQ7, 'x8').
Each transaction is a sequence of phases: instruction -> address (3 or 4 bytes) -> optional mode/alternate bits -> programmable dummy cycles -> data; each phase may use 1/2/4/8 lanes.
Protocol modes are written S-A-D (lanes per instruction/address/data): 1-1-1, 1-1-2, 1-2-2, 1-1-4, 1-4-4, 4-4-4 (QPI), 1-1-8, 1-8-8, 8-8-8 (SDR), 8D-8D-8D (octal DDR).
Dummy cycles absorb the device read latency between address/mode and data; their count is device- and frequency-dependent and configurable, and is discoverable via SFDP.

SDR launches/captures one bit per lane per SCLK cycle; DDR/DTR uses both SCLK edges. Octal DDR (8D-8D-8D) drives a source-synchronous Data Strobe (DQS) edge-aligned to read data for high-frequency capture.

A standard JEDEC flash command set is supported: Write Enable 0x06, Read Status 0x05, Fast Read 0x0B, Quad I/O Fast Read 0xEB, Quad Output 0x6B, Quad Page Program 0x32, Sector Erase 0x20, Block Erase 0xD8, Read JEDEC ID 0x9F, Read SFDP 0x5A.

SFDP (JESD216) self-describing parameter tables, read with 0x5A, expose density, supported read modes, dummy-cycle and mode-bit counts, erase types, and address bytes so a generic controller can auto-configure.
3-byte (24-bit, 16 MB) and 4-byte (32-bit, >16 MB) addressing are supported; 4-byte mode is entered with 0xB7 and exited with 0xE9, or via dedicated 4-byte opcodes.
Continuous Read Mode (mode/alternate bits) lets the next read skip the instruction phase, supporting eXecute-In-Place (XIP) code-shadow boot.
A program/erase requires Write Enable (0x06, sets WEL) first; the controller polls the Write In Progress (WIP) bit via Read Status (0x05) until the operation completes.
xSPI defines volatile and non-volatile configuration registers (protocol mode, dummy-cycle latency, DQS enable, address-byte count, drive strength) in addition to the legacy status registers.

error_response_conditions: WEL not set — a Page Program / Erase is ignored.
WIP busy — a new program/erase to a busy device is rejected; the controller must poll WIP.
Wrong dummy-cycle configuration — high-frequency multi-IO reads return corrupted data (the most common bring-up error).
Block/sector protection (BP) violation — a protected region rejects erase/program.
Unsupported opcode in the current protocol mode — device ignores it.
